newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Australia 10-yr bond yield breaks 7.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Australia 10-yr bond yield breaks 7.0 pct.

text.p: *The benchmark 10-year bond yield broke below the 7.0 barrier during the pre-weekend SYCOM session as the equivalent June futures contract overcame resistance at 93.015.
*The June position, touching it highest level since February 1994 in after hours trade, expires at midday.

The benchmark Australian 10-year bond yield made a clean break below the 7.0 percent barrier during the pre-weekend after hours session as the equivalent June futures contract overcame resistance at 93.015.
The June contract, which expires at midday, ended SYCOM at 93.035 having touched the market's highest level since February 1994 at 93.050 after overcoming the 93.015 December 1996 peak.
The contract, which ended Friday's pit session at 92.975, now has a target of 93.180, although this is more likely to be left for a test later this week by the incoming September front position.

The September position, which ended SYCOM at 92.980 and a 5.5 basis point discount to the June position, stands just above a support barrier of 92.950/92.970, although a firmer level is seen at 92.850, analysts said.
The market, which is already buoyed by expectation of a further easing in monetary policy, got a further boost from a weaker than expected U.S. PPI for May on Friday.

The PPI fell 0.3 percent when a 0.1 percent rise had been expected, and was a further piece of data which was seen lessening the chances of a tightening by the Federal Reserve when the Federal Open Market Committee meets on July 1/2.

The Reserve Bank holds its monthly board meeting on July 1, although the market is on alert for a policy announcement at any time given the the surprise timing of the last rate move to 5.5 percent on May 23.
The September bill futures contract is already more or less pricing in a 50 basis point easing at a SYCOM close of 94.91, which equates to a cash rate of 5.09 percent.

There is very little on the local data calendar this week, although there is plenty of U.S. data to get through, particularly on Tuesday when CPI, housing starts, industrial production and capacity utilisation for May are due.
